alerts.title: Abdominal pain on TLD: screen for ADR and assess cause
alerts.message: Guidelines require all health workers to screen every encounter for suspected adverse drug reactions using the Drug Safety Screening checklist, and to record and report any suspected ADR, mild or severe. Patient P004 has been on TDF, 3TC, DTG since March 2023 and presents with new abdominal pain without fever, with appetite preserved. The excerpts list abdominal-related and hypersensitivity/hepatic symptoms as ADR screening items, but the excerpts do not establish that abdominal pain is a specific attributable effect of TDF, 3TC, or DTG. Evidence against drug attribution includes the long stable course and absence of fever; the record does not document a lipase, liver panel, or abdominal assessment, so attribution cannot be determined from available data.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the Drug Safety Screening checklist for this encounter, document the abdominal pain features, and report any suspected ADR per the reporting pathway. Consider liver function and other clinically indicated tests to clarify the cause.
